title: From the supervisor, Dr. Rika Kayama
translation:
Up until now, it has been said that reality comes in two kinds: the external reality we can actually see with our own eyes, and the internal reality that exists only inside a person's heart. But with the advent of games, another kind of reality was born in the space between the two. I even believe that how humanity chooses to treat this newborn reality holds the key to our future.

This game, "Dyna Brothers," is packed full of the charm of that "in-between reality." The player gets to move freely through a world of dinosaurs, matching wits with aliens while protecting a precious environment. You will be the first person in the world to experience something like this - and you get to enjoy it while you're at it!

I'm sure that after playing in the dinosaurs' powerful world, you'll come away charged with unpredictable energy!

- Rika Kayama, psychiatrist and game lover

title: Dyna Brothers Story
translation:
An archaeologist discovered a cave deep in the jungle. Inside, astonishingly, lay buried ancient ruins. The walls of the ruins were covered in murals, and beneath the murals, ancient writing was carved, explaining them. It told the story of a great war from long, long ago.

"Jurassic Era, Year 1701
We, the five dinosaur tribes, helped one another and built a peaceful world in harmony with nature. The reason we were able to flourish was thanks to the blessing of The Egg, said to be the source of life, which first created the eggs.
One day, a huge black shadow covered the sky. From it, several great birds took flight and descended upon the land in various places."

What descended on every region were not birds, but spaceships carrying invaders.
The aliens that emerged from the ships suddenly attacked us.

We fought bravely, but against the invaders' overwhelming numbers, there was nothing we could do, and little by little we lost the fight.
And then, when only a single egg remained...

The Egg let out a dazzling light.

The Egg awoke, and a miracle happened.】

title: Control Pad Operation
translation:
Standard layout...... (can be changed on the Options screen)
A Button............ Switches between "Icon Control Mode" and "Zoomed Screen Control Mode." Holding it down switches from the normal "Icon Control Mode" to "Zoomed Screen Control Mode"; releasing the button returns you to normal.
B Button............ Cancel
C Button............ Confirm
Start Button........ (the game pauses)
Displays the "Status Screen."
(-> P.22)

[Icon Control Mode]
Use the D-Pad to select a command icon.
Press the C Button to execute the command.

[Zoomed Screen Control Mode]
Instead of command icons, the number of herbivores, carnivores, egg-eaters, and eggs for each side (yours and the enemy's) is displayed.
You can also scroll the zoomed screen with the D-Pad. Even in this mode, pressing the C Button will execute the currently selected command.

title: Character Introduction
translation:
Dyna Brothers Character Introduction

Tyranno (Offensive Carnivore)
Always a headstrong troublemaker.
He charges straight at any enemy and eats whoever he defeats. His one weak point is that he tends to get fixated on whatever's right in front of him.
He serves as the main force of your attack, fighting bravely.

Allo (Interceptor Carnivore)
A cool, swift, and highly skilled hunter.
Normally calm, but a bit of a fool once he gets worked up and loses himself. He doesn't move around much, instead swiftly catching enemies who come close. He guards the eggs around his own camp.
The natural enemy of egg-eaters.

title: Character Introduction (continued)
translation:
Pi-chan (Egg-eater)
Weak in a fight, but a quick runner and a bit of a clown.
He finds enemy eggs and sneaks off with a bite to eat.
He's a great runner, and if there's an egg to be had he'll dash all the way into enemy territory. With nimble footwork he dodges enemy carnivores, teasing and toying with them.

Tricera (Defensive Herbivore)
Normally laid-back, but a scary one once angered. He doesn't like conflict, but if attacked he believes in striking back, and when he's serious he can even take down carnivores. He doesn't lay many eggs, so he's hard to breed in large numbers.

Stego (Breeding Herbivore)
Quiet and easygoing. He loves basking in the sun while grazing on grass. He isn't strong, but he lays lots of eggs. Because he breeds easily, he becomes the main power source for The Egg.

title: Game Screen Explanation
translation:
Game Screen Explanation

1. Zoomed Screen
Displays the characters and background as they actually appear.
2. Overview Map
Shows the whole map and the locations of both allies and enemies.
3. Selected Command
Shows the currently selected command icon.
4. Power
Shows The Egg's current power value.
5. Command Icons
By executing these commands you can bring about various miracles.
The table below shows what is displayed in place of the command icons while in "Zoomed Screen Display Mode."

Number of allied herbivores / Number of enemy herbivores
Number of allied carnivores / Number of enemy carnivores
Number of allied egg-eaters / Number of enemy egg-eaters
Number of allied eggs / Number of enemy eggs

* When a number lights up red, it means that type of dinosaur has died.

title: Terrain Explanation
translation:
The terrain across which the dinosaurs move of their own will is fixed. If you want to move them onto other terrain, use the Individual Guidance command. However, since stamina consumption varies greatly depending on the terrain, be careful not to overwork your dinosaurs.

Grassland
Stamina consumption when moving is lowest here, and the dinosaurs roam freely. The grass changes through 4 stages depending on how much is growing. It thins out when herbivores eat it, but it grows back over time.

Bare Ground
Stamina consumption when moving is high here, so the dinosaurs will not step onto it on their own. If grassland is adjacent, you can make grass grow here by causing rain to fall.

title: Terrain Explanation (continued)
translation:
Wasteland
Stamina consumption is low, but no matter how much rain falls, grass will never grow on this land, so herbivores won't move here on their own. Carnivores and egg-eaters will walk across it.

River, Sea
Anyone other than herbivores uses up a great deal of stamina here. If stamina runs low, they will drown. They won't enter unless guided there. Also, grassland tends to spread more easily near the water's edge.

Bottomless Swamp
Any dinosaur can drown here. The dinosaurs won't enter on their own, but if one lies in the path of Individual Guidance, they will get stuck in it. Guide them carefully.

title: Terrain Explanation (continued)
translation:
Trees (Flammable)
This is an obstacle, so it cannot be crossed. Dinosaurs in its path will go around it. However, it will burn and turn into bare ground if hit by the flames from a Meteor.

Rocks (Non-flammable)
This is an obstacle, so it cannot be crossed. However, unlike trees, it will not burn even from a Meteor's flames.

Fire
When a Meteor falls, it starts a fire, which spreads rapidly across grass and trees. Any living creature burns instantly. The fire goes out naturally when it reaches the water's edge, but it can also be put out with rain or a flood.

As the stages progress, the background will change. Also, when events like a drought wipe out all the grass, every creature will seek out grassland, sometimes moving onto terrain they normally wouldn't enter.

title: Command Icon Explanation
translation:
Rain Command
Within the zoomed screen, you can make it rain only around your own dinosaurs. If rain falls on bare ground next to grassland, grass will spread onto it. Rain falling on grassland also speeds up the growth of the grass.

Guidance Command
There are two types: Group Guidance, which sets a movement direction for all your herbivores at once, and Individual Guidance, which guides a specific dinosaur to a destination. (-> P.18)

Egg Creation Command
Produces a dinosaur egg from The Egg. You can choose from 5 species. (-> P.19)
This command cannot be used unless there is grassland around The Egg.

Egg Modification Command
Uses radiation to change the species of one of your eggs. The selection method is the same as Egg Creation. Changing the species requires the new species' egg cost plus a 1000-yen handling fee.

title: Command Icon Explanation (continued)
translation:
Disaster Command
Using the power gathered from your dinosaurs' life energy, you can trigger various disasters to attack the enemy. (-> P.20)

The Egg Command
No matter where the zoomed screen currently is, selecting this command instantly moves the zoomed screen to The Egg's location.

Marking Command
Marks a specific unit you want to keep track of, or an enemy UFO. Only one target can be marked at a time. The enemy may also mark your dinosaurs or The Egg.

Catch Command
Instantly moves the zoomed screen to the character marked with the Marking command.
(Cannot be used if nothing is currently marked.)

title: How to Use the Guidance Command
translation:
1. Group Guidance (does not consume Power)

Group Guidance Icon
"Guides all your herbivores." When you specify a direction, your herbivores gradually move in that direction, a little at a time. Use it mainly to point them toward where you want grassland to spread.

Group Guidance Stop Icon
While Group Guidance is active, selecting this stop icon will cancel it.

2. Individual Guidance (consumes 3 yen of Power per turn while guiding)

Individual Guidance Icon
"Select one of your dinosaurs and guide it to a specified destination." A dinosaur under Individual Guidance will first move diagonally until it reaches a position where it can head straight toward the destination either vertically/horizontally, then proceed in a straight line. It will push straight through terrain it would not normally cross, such as bare ground or sea. It will avoid obstacles like trees and rocks. Be careful not to let it fall into the sea, a swamp, or similar hazards.

Individual Guidance Stop Icon
While Individual Guidance is active, selecting this icon will cancel it.

title: How to Use the Egg Creation Command
translation:
Since each species of dinosaur has different abilities, creating the right dinosaur for the situation -- offense, defense, and so on -- is a key part of the game.

Stego (300 yen)
Has high life energy, so making plenty of them early on helps increase The Egg's power.

Tricera (300 yen)
Hard to breed, but strong, so it's worth keeping a few around for defense.

Tyranno (800 yen)
Once created, he'll head straight for the enemy on his own. Make plenty of them in the late game when it's time to settle things.

Allo (800 yen)
Won't move until he spots an enemy, but is powerful on defense, so keep a few on hand by the midgame, once the enemy starts attacking.

Pi-chan (1000 yen)
He hunts for enemy eggs to eat, so sending him into enemy territory can give you a big advantage. Watch out for the enemy's Interceptor Carnivores, though.

title: How to Use Disaster Attacks
translation:
These disasters only occur within the zoomed screen. They affect both allies and enemies without distinction, so be careful not to catch your own dinosaurs in them. Also, they are not guaranteed to affect everything on screen.

Lightning (1000 yen)
"Gathers electrical energy from the atmosphere to generate lightning."
The electric shock instantly hatches eggs. Use it when you've made lots of eggs and want to hatch them all at once, or when your eggs are about to be eaten.

Drought (2000 yen)
"Gathers solar energy from the atmosphere and beams it down."
The heat of the sun withers plants, instantly turning grassland into bare ground. Use it around an enemy UFO, and the enemy will be unable to create eggs there for a while.

title: How to Use Disaster Attacks (continued)
translation:
Earthquake (2000 yen)
"Injects life energy into the earth's crust to trigger an earthquake."
The earthquake destroys eggs. It's effective when the enemy has made a lot of eggs, or when they're making a carnivore's egg.

Flood (4000 yen)
"Gathers moisture from the atmosphere to cause a flood."
The flood washes creatures away. If the enemy has gathered in large numbers, wipe them all out at once.

Meteor (8000 yen)
"Calls down a shooting star from space."
Where it lands catches fire. Trees and grassland will catch and spread the flames. It will keep burning unless put out with rain or a flood. It extinguishes naturally at the water's edge.

title: Status Screen Explanation
translation:
Pressing the Start button during the game temporarily pauses it and brings up the Status Screen, showing a large view of the overview map. Pressing the A button lets you switch to the screens below.

'TERRAIN DATA'
Shows the types of terrain. You can see the layout of grassland, rocks, bottomless swamps, and so on across the map. Use it as reference for strategy.

'CREATURE MAP'
Shows where your dinosaurs and the enemy aliens are located. Since species can be told apart by color, you can get a sense of the overall balance of power.

title: Information Display Screen
translation:
'Egg Map'
Shows you where eggs are located. Eggs are displayed at different sizes depending on how far along their growth is.

'Surrender'
Select this when you want to end the game partway through. Pressing the C Button in this state brings up a confirmation message. Pressing the C Button again will cause you to surrender.

title: Activating the Finale
translation:
If it takes too long to defeat the aliens, their environmental reformation device will activate, triggering the Finale and causing natural disasters to occur. There's no telling what kind of changes will happen, but in any case, conditions will become even harsher for the dinosaurs than before.
Even after the Finale has been triggered, you can still advance to the next stage by wiping out the aliens, but if at all possible, it's better to defeat the enemy before that happens.

For example...

Rising Sea Levels
The sea level gradually rises. Eventually, the dinosaurs will be swallowed up by the sea, land and all.

Ice Age
The land becomes covered entirely in snow, and grass stops growing. The dinosaurs will die off one after another from cold and starvation.

Various other kinds of Finales can also occur.

title: How the Game Proceeds
translation:
You play as The Egg, now awakened. Before the environmental reformation devices inside the UFOs stationed around the map can activate, defeat the aliens guarding each UFO and destroy their environmental reformation device.

Use the power you're given at the start to create herbivores and increase their numbers. The Egg automatically absorbs power from the dinosaurs through them. Use the power gained from the growing number of dinosaurs to create carnivores and egg-eaters. Also, use natural disaster attacks to defeat the aliens. Defeating all the aliens is the objective of this game. Once you defeat all the aliens, you can advance to the next stage, which has a different front-line base.

Game End Conditions
The game ends when either your dinosaurs or the enemy aliens are completely wiped out.
1. When you defeat all enemy aliens
   The stage is cleared and you advance to the next round.
2. When all your dinosaurs are defeated
   It's Game Over.
3. When the player chooses to 'Surrender'
   It's Game Over.

title: [Stage 1] How to Make Eggs, How to Make It Rain
translation:
This stage gives you plenty of power from the start, so feel free to try out various commands.
Now, let's explain the basic controls and strategic procedure common to all stages, using Stage 1 as an example.

1. Egg Creation (First, create herbivore eggs.)
- Use the Directional Buttons to move the finger cursor onto the Egg Creation icon and press the C Button; a dinosaur icon will be displayed.
- Use the finger cursor to choose a herbivore ('Stego' or 'Tricera'), and press the C Button to confirm; an egg will be laid.
- 'Stego' is weak but multiplies quickly. 'Tricera' is strong but doesn't multiply much. Create them according to the situation.

title: Making Eggs, Making Rain (continued)
translation:
- If you keep holding the C Button, as long as you have power, the same type of egg will keep being laid one after another. Try making about 8 of them here as a test.
  (You can create as many eggs as there are grassland tiles around The Egg. The maximum you can create at once is 8.)
- Pressing the B Button returns you to the original selection screen.
After a while, the dinosaurs will hatch from their eggs and begin moving around freely.

2. Making It Rain. (Use the Rain command to expand the grassland.)
- Hold the A Button and use the Directional Buttons to freely move the zoomed-in view.
- Use this to follow the dinosaurs around and observe them for a bit.
- If you spot a dinosaur next to a patch of bare ground, make it rain there.
- Release the A Button, select the Rain command icon, and press the C Button. It will rain.
- When rain falls on ground next to grassland, the grass spreads to cover it. Also, making it rain on grassland speeds up the grass's growth. If there isn't enough grass and the herbivores are struggling, make it rain. If left alone, they may starve to death.

title: Raising Herbivores, Carnivore Attacks
translation:
3. Raise herbivores to build up power.
Normally, from here you would keep making eggs and making it rain to expand the grassland, steadily increasing your herbivores to build up power. In this stage, you already have plenty of power, so once you're tired of raising herbivores, feel free to attack at any time.

4. Attacks by carnivores
Once you've secured enough grassland for around 10 herbivores to live freely, try using the Egg Creation command to create a 'Tyranno' egg.

- Once hatched, 'Tyranno' heads straight for the enemy aliens.
- 'Tyranno' only walks on grassland and wasteland, so when it reaches the edge of the grassland, make it rain to expand the grassland and create a path for it.
- When launching an all-out assault, keep making eggs as fast as you can build up the power for them.

title: Egg-Eater Attacks, Carnivore Defense
translation:
5. Attacks by egg-eaters
If you have power to spare, try making a 'Pi-chan'.
- 'Pi-chan' doesn't attack the enemy directly, but it eats the aliens' eggs, which holds back their breeding and power growth. It also draws the attention of the aliens' attack-type carnivorous aliens, so it can buy you time as well.
- Just like with 'Tyranno', make it rain to create a path and guide it toward the eggs.

6. Defense with carnivores
When it looks like enemy carnivorous or egg-eating aliens are about to attack, create 'Allo' early to protect the area around The Egg.
- 'Allo' attacks and defeats any enemy that comes near. It won't go on the offensive by itself. Ideally, you should keep 1 or 2 of them around The Egg at all times.
- If an enemy egg-eating alien is about to attack before 'Allo's' egg looks ready to hatch, use the 'Lightning' natural disaster command to hatch the egg.

title: Q&A Corner
translation:
1. I have power, but I can't create an egg. Why is that?
-> You need open space around The Egg for an egg to be laid. Either wait for an existing egg to hatch and clear the space, or move whatever creature is occupying it.

2. My own dinosaurs are fighting each other. Why is that?
-> Carnivores and egg-eaters will attack and eat even their own allies when they get hungry, in order to survive. It's a tough position for them too. Please understand.

3. My power suddenly dropped a lot. Why?
-> That's because one of your dinosaurs died somewhere. In particular, when a 'Pi-chan' or a carnivore dies, your power drops by a large amount, so be careful.

4. Who's that surfing?
-> That's the 'Pi-chan' Surfing Team. Don't worry about it too much — just enjoy the music.

5. What's a 'King Tyranno'?
-> ...You'll have to find out for yourself.

title: Enemy Characters
translation:
The enemy aliens, just like the Dyna Brothers, include herbivorous aliens, carnivorous aliens, and egg-eating aliens. Each species has a mostly similar temperament. New characters appear as you progress through the stages. Let's introduce a few of them here.

Pugupen (Breeding-type herbivorous alien)
A glutton and a coward. Skilled at the 'wiggling-butt dodge.'

Gumi Gumi-chan (Breeding-type herbivorous alien)
An amoeba-like creature that multiplies rapidly. Its attack power is low, but during battle it can freely reshape its body depending on whether it's attacking or defending.

Kunerin (Defense-type herbivorous alien)
The guard dog of the alien army. Counterattacks with a biting attack and an eye-beam. Turns vicious when angered.

title: Enemy Characters (continued)
translation:
Jamera (Attack-type carnivorous alien)
A powerful meathead who unleashes his finishing move, the 'Great Spinning Slap.' Not very bright, so he fights by brute force.

Pekipekiman (Defense-type herbivorous alien)
Has many finishing moves and the makings of a leader, but is timid at heart, so he ends up doing menial work.

Lady Kurara (Interception-type carnivorous alien)
Technically female. Her graceful walk is charming. Both smart and tough, she has the unreliable alien army wrapped around her finger.

Kiraran (Egg-eating-type alien)
Has the 'Kiraran Attack,' which uses her charming eyes to mesmerize opponents, but it rarely seems to actually work.

title: Dr. Rika Kayama's Personality Diagnosis
translation:
Who's your favorite character in Dyna Brothers? Dr. Rika Kayama will diagnose your personality based on your answer.

Tyranno
You're the reliable type who believes in taking charge of your own life. But you also have a vulnerable side — you surprisingly worry about what others think of you.

Allo
With your iron will, people around you secretly think of you as 'mysterious, but someone to keep an eye on.' The day your true talent blossoms all at once isn't far off. Don't lose your own pace.

title: Dr. Rika Kayama's Personality Diagnosis (continued)
translation:
Pi-chan
You're sensitive to information and trends — truly a trendy person who fits right into modern society. You might be told you don't stick with things for long, but hey, having fun is what matters most in life!

Tricera
A type common among lovers of starry skies and plants. You might be misunderstood as difficult to deal with, but really you're very kind. You don't have many friends, but you're the type to stick with the ones you have, through thick and thin.

Stego
Deep down, don't you sometimes think 'I'm no good anyway...'? Others may see you as a good-natured, understanding person, but once in a while, go ahead and stand out a little.

title: The Master's Winning Tips
translation:
First, let the master himself lay out a few key points about the game, so pay close attention and remember them well.

- Keep a close watch on enemy movements. At the start, we recommend marking the UFOs.
- Which direction you expand the grassland greatly affects later battles. Sometimes it's better not to expand it too much.
- You need to create herbivores with the size of the grassland in mind. Creating too many in a cramped area just leads to starvation from food shortages.
- Individual Guidance is the only way to move a dinosaur exactly where you want it. Mastering its use is itself a strategy.
- Once your herbivores have bred, Egg Modification is effective — it lets you launch surprise carnivore attacks from unexpected places.
- 'Meteor' isn't just for attacking. It can also change the terrain by burning away trees. However, please be extremely careful with fire.
- The enemy's thinking ability and attack methods change depending on the stage. Each stage requires its own strategy.
- The further you progress, the more quick, decisive input becomes the key to not letting the enemy seize the initiative — that, above all, is the ultimate winning strategy.

title: The Master's Winning Tips (continued)
translation:
In Dyna Brothers, only 5 kinds of allied creatures appear, but depending on how you use them, you can fight with all sorts of strategies. Here are a few examples for reference — but I encourage you to research others on your own.

The Stego Ranch
Normally, relying only on 'Stego' won't win you the game, but by taking advantage of safe terrain and deliberately breeding large numbers of 'Stego,' which has a high power growth rate, you can stockpile power. After that, it's an all-out counterattack using natural disaster commands.

The 'Pi-chan' Decoy
Deliberately guide 'Pi-chan' to a spot far from the battlefield. The enemy's attack-type carnivorous aliens will be drawn to it, buying you time. There's also a dirty trick where you lure enemies that gather around 'Pi-chan' and wipe them all out at once with 'Flood.'

One-Shot Hatching with 'Lightning'
When an enemy egg-eating alien approaches, lure it right up to 'Allo's' egg, then hatch it with 'Lightning' at just the right moment. This way, the enemy egg-eating alien becomes food for the newly hatched 'Allo.' However, if your timing is off, or if 'Lightning' misfires, you'll be handing the enemy an expensive (1800 En) meal, so aim carefully.

title: Winning Tips Continued: Special Edition
translation:
The Ultimate Defense Corps: The 'Allo' Squad
If you keep deploying more and more 'Allo' around The Egg, they'll line up at regular intervals, forming an invincible 'Allo Squad.' It's recommended to regularly supply 'Stego' as food for them. However, even this invincible squad can be wiped out instantly by a natural disaster attack, so don't rely on it too much.

The 'Drought' Panic
If an area surrounded by sea or bottomless swamp is crawling with enemies, it's drought season. If even a little grassland remains, hit it repeatedly. Enemies who suddenly lose their footing panic — jumping into the water, starving to death, and generally causing chaos, which is a lot of fun to watch. But don't overdo it, or people might think you're cruel.

These are just a few examples of ways to play Dyna Brothers. If you discover new strategies or something amazing, please do send a letter to the Master.

From the Mysterious Man from Kansai, Master Nagasato

title: Precautions for Use
translation:
The cartridge is a precision device, so please pay particular attention to the following:

First, Confirm the Power Is OFF!
Always make sure the console's power switch is set to OFF before inserting or removing the cartridge. Forcing the cartridge in or out while the power switch is ON may cause malfunction.

The Cartridge Is Delicate
Do not subject the cartridge to strong shocks. Do not strike or step on it. Also, never disassemble it.

Do Not Touch the Connector Pins
Touching the cartridge's connector pins, or getting them wet, may cause malfunction, so please be careful.

Do Not Wipe With Chemicals
When wiping dirt off the cartridge, do not use chemicals such as thinner or benzine.

title: Precautions for Use (continued)
translation:
Be Careful Where You Store It
When storing the cartridge, avoid places that are extremely hot or cold. Avoid locations in direct sunlight, near a heater, or with high humidity, as these are also to be avoided.

When Playing the Game
Playing games for long periods tires your eyes. For your health, please take a 10-20 minute break every hour while playing. Also, please play at a reasonable distance from the TV screen.

Do not connect the Mega Drive to a projection TV (a screen-projection-type television), as afterimage burn-in may occur on the screen.
